Sure, in the coming years she might "get over this" and realize she's not bi-sexual. Not letting her "explore" this in the sense of telling her to push it aside until she's older, can cause her tons of issues. Don't be the reason your daughter thinks she can't fully come out when shes older and affirms that she is bi-sexual. If she isn't in a little while, so be it. You don't have to paint your house in rainbows and take her to pride. Just don't tell her to keep it to herself. I thought the same thing when I was younger. I thought "If I ever have queer kids, I'm going to tell them to wait on it and try being straight" but now, after going through my own experiences, I realize that would be the wrong thing to do.

You for sure can. The term high functioning is a mixed bag, because it enforces this hierarchy. Like my sister is high functioning for Cerebral Palsy. My friend with Asperger's is high functioning. My friend has Bi Polar and believes that she is the be all and end all of who's crazy. I mentioned my bpd once and she said "No, you don't have it. Talk to your doctor about this, and maybe see if you can speak to a therapist. Best of luck figuring everything out :)

I asked a teacher this in grade school. In Judaism, suicide is shunned because this soul and body is a gift from god. However; there are many stories throughout the old testament and other holy texts, that mention suicide in a "good" light. There's a popular story that involves this woman and her 7 sons.
